Do you want to lead 10 engineers building a Legal-Tech SaaS platform on .NET and Azure?

At Epona in Vejle, you will lead the engineering organization behind our Legal-Tech SaaS platform, used by more than 800 law firms and corporate legal departments worldwide. Our platform is built with .NET 10, C#, Azure services, REST APIs and semantic search.

You will combine people leadership with accountability for reliable delivery, engineering quality and continuous improvement, while helping Epona transition from its existing solution to the next-generation SaaS platform.

Your teams

You will be responsible for 10 engineers in Vejle, organized in three teams:

• Two agile product development teams, one working on our new SaaS platform and one on the on-premise solution it replaces

• One platform team of two DevOps engineers, owning CI/CD, infrastructure (Terraform) and cloud operations

How we work with AI

AI is part of how we work, both as product capabilities and as tooling in our engineering workflow. We use Claude as a coding companion to accelerate product delivery and improve quality. We expect you to drive effective and critical use of AI tools across your teams.

Promote responsible AI adoption, including security, code review, testing and appropriate human oversight. Assess its impact on delivery speed, quality and developer effectiveness rather than measuring usage alone.

Your role

As the Head of Engineering, your primary focus is on people leadership and delivering results through your teams. You bring a strong technical background that enables you to challenge technical decisions, contribute to architectural discussions and ensure engineering quality. You report to the CTO.

• Lead, coach and develop 10 engineers through 1:1s, feedback and career development

• Set clear expectations, provide regular performance feedback, address underperformance and develop succession and capability plans.

• Make AI tools like Claude part of how the teams work, and measure the effect on delivery

• Ensure predictable, high-quality delivery with Product Management, including AI-powered capabilities in our platform

• Translate agreed product priorities into realistic engineering commitments; make risks, dependencies, trade-offs and capacity constraints visible early.

• Use relevant indicators such as lead time, delivery predictability, defect trends, reliability and incident resolution to drive improvement, not reporting for its own sake.

• Drive technical direction and engineering quality together with architects and senior engineers

• Strengthen automated testing, security, scalability, maintainability, CI/CD and management of technical debt.

• Collaborate with international colleagues and shape team structure and ways of working across product and platform teams

• Partner with Operations and Support to identify recurring customer issues, reduce avoidable incidents and feed insights into engineering and product improvements.

• Communicate decisions, progress and risks transparently and follow through on agreed actions across teams.

• Own how and how well we deliver, including technical trade-offs and delivery commitments. The Project Manager owns what we deliver and why. Timelines are agreed jointly by trading off scope, time and quality, with escalation to CPO and CTO.

• Stay technically involved through occasional code reviews and technical contributions, while playing a key role in architectural decisions alongside architects and senior engineers. The primary focus remains on leading the engineering teams rather than individual coding.

Measuring success

Success will be measured through improvements in AI adoption and impact, engineering delivery and quality, team engagement and retention, and collaboration with Product Management and Operations.

Within the first 60 days, you will establish baselines and agree measurable 6- and 12-month improvement targets with the CTO.

How you lead – Epona values

Epona’s five values guide how we lead, make decisions and work together. The Engineering Manager is expected to demonstrate them through visible behaviour, not just words.

• One Team — Build a shared identity across Engineering, Product, Operations and Support. Break down silos, actively help colleagues, and put shared outcomes ahead of “them and us” thinking.

• Customer First — Make quality and delivery central to engineering decisions. Understand customer impact, address recurring issues and prioritise reliable outcomes for customers.

• Transparency — Explain the why behind decisions, priorities and trade-offs. Communicate progress, risks and changes openly so teams understand both the direction and the reasoning.

• Responsible — Deliver on promises, take ownership of mistakes, and make responsibilities and follow-up explicit. Combine flexibility and autonomy with clear accountability.

• Respect — Respect cultural differences and individual perspectives. Give feedback respectfully, invite constructive challenge and build an inclusive, supportive team environment.

Tech stack

• Backend and data: .NET 10, C#, MS SQL Server / Azure SQL, Entity Framework Core

• Cloud: Azure (Functions, Web Apps, API Management, Front Door, Entra ID, etc.)

• AI and search: Claude as coding companion, AI-powered product capabilities, Azure AI Search (semantic/vector search)

• DevOps and testing: Azure Pipelines, Terraform, xUnit

• Integrations: SharePoint

What we’re looking for

• 3+ years as an Head of Engineering or Team Lead with direct reports

• A background as a software engineer, preferably in .NET/C# and Azure

• Daily use of AI coding tools, and experience getting a team to adopt them

• Knowledge of how AI features are built and run in production

• Experience building teams that ship SaaS reliably

• Fluent in English (Danish is a plus, not required)

• Proven people leadership, including coaching, performance management and building accountable, collaborative teams.

• Ability to balance technical excellence with business priorities and customer outcomes; communicate trade-offs constructively.

• Nice to have: experience with Terraform and Azure Pipelines, semantic search, SharePoint integrations, Legal-Tech or other regulated industries.

What we offer

• Flexible hybrid setup: 3 days on-site in Vejle, 2 days remote

• Competitive salary matching your experience

• International environment

• Leadership and professional development through sparring, courses and conferences

• An opportunity to shape the next-generation SaaS engineering organisation and its ways of working.

About Epona

Epona is a global Legal-Tech company delivering intelligent document, email and case management solutions built on Microsoft and .NET technology. With offices in the Netherlands, Portugal, USA and Denmark, we serve more than 800 clients worldwide.

How to apply

You can apply via 'Apply' below, but in case you have questions, feel free to reach out to HR via the email address: hr@epona.com.

Application deadline: No fixed deadline. We review applications on an ongoing basis.

Epona is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

**Turn scientific promise into clinical progress. Build the proof-of-concept engine that helps LEO Pharma make smarter development decisions and bring meaningful innovation closer to patients.

****Shape What Comes Next

**How would you connect emerging biology, quantitative insights, and clinical expertise to shape the next generation of development programs? At LEO Pharma, you will lead Translational Medicine & Early Development, bringing together people, partners, and evidence to answer critical questions early. This is an opportunity to build capabilities, influence portfolio decisions, and connect scientific ambition with a clear path to clinical proof of concept.

**Your role

**You will build and lead an integrated proof-of-concept engine, translating biological hypotheses into clinically testable, quantitatively informed, decision-ready programs. Working across internal teams and external partners, you will establish mechanism-based rationales, meaningful patient strategies, and robust development plans. Your focus will be on generating the evidence needed to select doses, assess benefit–risk, and guide progression toward registrational studies.

Your primary responsibilities will be to:

• Lead translational and early-development strategy across programs, developing people leaders and subject-matter experts.

• Partner with Science, Search & Innovation and clinical teams to design early-phase studies demonstrating target engagement, proof of mechanism, and patient relevance.

• Integrate biomarkers, patient stratification, quantitative pharmacology, and modelling and simulation to optimize doses, regimens, endpoints, and study designs.

• Support clinical due diligence and integration of externally sourced assets, building partnerships that strengthen translational capabilities.

• Shape regulatory and cross-functional evidence strategies, translating complex findings into clear recommendations for project teams and governance forums.

You will also establish progression criteria and performance indicators that strengthen decision quality, evidence maturity, execution, and resource efficiency. Throughout early development, you will ensure efficacy hypotheses are considered alongside safety, tolerability, and therapeutic index.

**Your Qualifications

**You bring scientific depth and leadership experience, with the ability to connect translational evidence to clinical and portfolio decisions.

We are looking for:

• An advanced degree in Medicine, Pharmacology, Translational Science, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related discipline; MD and PhD qualifications are preferred.

• Significant leadership experience in translational medicine, clinical pharmacology, and/or early clinical development within biotech or pharma.

• Demonstrated expertise in early-phase studies in patients and healthy participants, linking mechanisms of action and biomarkers to dose selection and development strategy.

• A track record of building high-performing global teams, developing people, and integrating external assets and partnerships.

• Experience contributing to regulatory submissions and evidence generation supporting registration and market access.

Experience with externally sourced innovation is strongly preferred; dermatology and/or rare-disease experience is beneficial. You combine strategic thinking with curiosity, sound judgment, and a collaborative approach, influencing effectively across a matrix organization.

**Your new team

**You will lead Translational Medicine & Early Development, with two line managers as direct reports, the group is in total 20 employees. You will report to the Vice President, Head of Global Clinical Development.

Your network will span clinical development, skin science, regulatory, safety, market access, and commercial colleagues. Together with external collaborators, you will connect expertise across disciplines to strengthen early development.

Board Intelligence is a technology and advisory firm on a mission to make boards more effective, and through them, build better businesses and benefit society.

Over twenty years we have established ourselves as the market leader in governance and board effectiveness, trusted by more than 80,000 directors, executives, and governance professionals globally, including across the Fortune 500, FTSE 100, and OMX 30. That trust has been earned through depth of insight, rigorous advisory work, and a track record that newer entrants simply cannot replicate.

We have invested in applied AI since 2020, well ahead of the market, and that early conviction has paid off. Our AI-powered platform and smart board advisor give us a competitive advantage that is widening, not narrowing. In 2024, K1 Investment Management, the leading B2B Enterprise SaaS investor, backed us to accelerate that position further. We are now growing fast, with a proven commercial model spanning both mid-market and enterprise, and a product suite that has become a necessary addition in high-stakes board environments.

The people joining us now will shape how we scale. We are deliberate about how we do that. Our founders and leadership team are deeply invested in keeping the culture that got us here: thoughtful, high calibre, and genuinely human. Ambition and balance are not in competition at Board Intelligence.

If you want to work at the intersection of AI and governance, on problems that matter at the highest level, this is a strong place to be.

Our Mission

**The Role

Clients include PwC, Bird & Bird and Bech-Bruun. Juristic is now part of Board Intelligence, and we are bringing a new product to market. The work is led by our CTO, and we are looking for an AI Engineer to build it with them from the first line of code.

This is a zero-to-one role in a small team of four full-stack developers, a machine learning engineer and the CTO. You will write the code, sit in front of customers, and help decide what we build next.

**Main Responsibilities

**

• Design, build and ship the AI capabilities at the core of a new product, from first prototype to production

• Own LLM-powered workflows end to end, such as document understanding, data extraction and agentic assistants

• Choose and integrate models and providers, and own the prompting, retrieval, evaluation and guardrails that make AI output reliable enough for legal and governance work

• Work directly with customers and the CTO to turn real problems into product decisions, and help own the product roadmap

• Lay the engineering foundations for the new product, including architecture, testing, observability and deployment, so it can scale

• Work with the wider Juristic and Board Intelligence engineering teams, and contribute to AI tooling shared across the suite

**Person Specification

**We are looking for a builder: an experienced AI engineer who has been a technical founder or an early employee at a startup, and who is ready to do it again.

Required Skills and Experience:

• At least four years of professional software engineering experience

• Experience as a technical founder or early employee at a startup, having built a product from the first line of code

• A track record of building and shipping AI or LLM-powered products to real users

• Practical experience with LLM APIs, prompt design, retrieval and evaluating model output in production

• Strong engineering fundamentals across backend and frontend, with the judgement to move fast without leaving a mess behind

• A strong product mindset: you have worked directly with customers and owned a product roadmap

• Hungry, motivated and ready for another zero-to-one journey

• Fluent written and spoken English

Nice to haves:

Experience with our stack: TypeScript (Node.js and React) and Python

Experience with document processing, such as PDF parsing and extraction from unstructured text

Experience building agentic systems, tool use or MCP integrations

Experience with search and retrieval infrastructure, such as Elasticsearch or vector databases

A background in legal tech, governance or B2B SaaS for professional users

What good looks like in this role:

• After three months: you know our customers, the product vision and the codebase, and you have shipped AI features that real users rely on

• After six months: the core AI capabilities of the new product are in production, backed by evaluations that show they are reliable, and you are acting on customer feedback

• After twelve months: the product is in market with paying customers, you are a trusted voice on the roadmap, and the AI foundations you built are reused across the Juristic and Board Intelligence suite

**How We Work

**We hire people who are expert at what they do. Once you join, you have the autonomy to shape how you work and the space to do it well. That doesn’t mean working in isolation. You’ll have colleagues who know their craft, regular collaboration across functions, and easy access to senior leadership when you need it.

We keep our structure flat. We work at pace in an agile, nimble environment where good ideas don’t wait for permission. If you spot something that could work better, we encourage you to say so. If you want to run with an idea, we’ll back you to do it.

We work with people who take pride in their output, back their team through the hard parts, and leave things better than they found them.

**What Happens Next

**Once you apply, our Talent team will review your application. If there’s a fit, they’ll be in touch to discuss the role and next steps.

**How We Use AI In Our Hiring

**We use AI responsibly, both in the software we build for governance teams and in how we hire. Our Talent team may use AI to support application review, CV analysis, or identifying areas that need further verification.

But hiring decisions are made by people. AI surfaces signals; people make the call on whether to progress a candidate or extend an offer.

If you’d like details on how your data is handled during recruitment, contact our Talent team.

**Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

**We’re an equal opportunities employer. We’re building a team that works because it reflects a breadth of experience, background, and perspective.

Apply even if you don’t tick every box on the job specification. If the role excites you and you think you could make an impact, we want to hear from you.

We don’t discriminate on the basis of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. If you need reasonable adjustments at any stage of recruitment, or if there’s anything else we can do to make the process more accessible, tell our Talent team. We’ll sort it.

**Your Safety Matters

**Be cautious of unexpected messages claiming to be from Board Intelligence. We will never ask you for fees as part of recruitment. If you’re unsure whether a communication is genuine, contact our Talent team through our official channels before sharing information or clicking links.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. jobs.description:
About Octarine

Octarine Bio is a Copenhagen-based biotech company making safe, sustainable, bio-based pigments. Our PurePalette™ platform uses precision fermentation and renewable raw materials to produce colourants that can replace petrochemical and mined pigments.

We are a team of around 15 people, working across pigment manufacturing, formulation and application development, and commercial development. As our pigment manufacturing processes reach full commercial scale, and our first pigment products are now in the hands of customers and partners, we are looking for someone with deep domain expertise in one or more of our core application areas (dyeing, printing, coatings and plastics) to make PurePalette™ work in real industrial applications and turn successful customer trials into lasting commercial products.

The role

You will be the technical owner of the PurePalette™ product range and the link between our lab and our customers. You will translate what the market needs into clear performance targets, work with our scientists to meet them, and make sure our pigment products perform once they reach a customer's processes.

We are looking for an applications expert in inks and coatings, plastics, or both, or in a closely related pigment application field. The title and scope will match your experience:

• Technical Product Specialist if you are earlier in your career and want a role with a lot of room to grow as the company scales.

• Head of Product Development if you have the experience to lead the product and applications function, shape the product roadmap and build a team.

In both cases you will report directly to our Chief Scientific Officer and work closely with our commercial team.

What you will do

Own the product, technically

• Be the technical expert for all PurePalette™ products and the first point of contact for technical questions from customers, partners and colleagues.

• Define the performance and quality parameters customers expect in each application, such as colour strength, dispersibility, heat stability, light and weather fastness, migration, rheology, and wash and rub fastness.

• Plan and coordinate the internal and external testing needed to prove each parameter, and turn the results into clear data packages for customers.

• Own, write and maintain our technical and product documentation, including Safety Data Sheets (SDS), Technical Data Sheets (TDS), Certificates of Analysis (CoA), product specifications and application guides.

Make our pigments work for customers

• Work with customers, distributors and partners to implement PurePalette™ products in their processes, from first lab trial to production run.

• Own the technical side of our partnerships with masterbatchers, ink manufacturers, dyehouses and research institutes. Set up project plans, manage technology transfer between parties, and troubleshoot problems until the product works in the target application.

• Handle technical customer feedback and complaints, find the root cause and feed lessons back into product and process development.

Decide what to develop next

• Identify where bio-based pigments offer real value to end users, and where they can genuinely meet customers' performance expectations.

• Work with Octarine scientists to map which applications our current pigments suit, and which applications we should target with future products.

• Work with our formulation and application scientists to refine formulations (dispersions, masterbatches, inks, dye and print pastes) to meet customer requirements.

• Work with our R&D and process teams to develop and implement strategies that improve pigment performance, for example through stabilisation, surface treatment or particle engineering.

• Benchmark our products against incumbent pigments and competing bio-based alternatives.

Connect technical and commercial

• Act as the bridge between Octarine's technical and commercial teams, translating customer needs into technical requirements and technical results into customer value.

• Join customer meetings, site visits and trade fairs as the technical voice of the company.

• Contribute technical content to sales materials, grant applications and investor discussions, and help capture new inventions for our IP portfolio.

What you bring

Pigment applications are many markets, not one. Printing inks alone span flexo, gravure, offset, screen and digital printing, and each places different demands on a pigment. The end markets differ just as much, from packaging and textiles to toys, consumer goods and coatings, each with its own performance, safety and regulatory requirements.

We need someone who knows this landscape in depth. You should understand the technical and performance requirements of each sub-application and market, judge where our pigments have a realistic and valuable fit, and work with our scientists to develop products that meet those requirements.

Specifically, we are looking for:

• An MSc or PhD in chemistry, polymer or materials science, chemical engineering, colour science or a related field, or equivalent industrial experience.

• Hands-on industrial experience applying pigments or colourants in textiles, inks and coatings, plastics and masterbatch, or a closely related field. For the Head of Product Development level, we expect around 5 or more years, including leading projects or people.

• A practical understanding of pigment dispersion and of how pigment properties such as particle size, surface chemistry and thermal stability affect performance in the final product.

• Experience with colour measurement (spectrophotometry, CIELAB, ΔE) and with standard ISO, EN or ASTM test methods for pigment and application performance.

• Experience writing or maintaining SDS, TDS and CoA documents, and working knowledge of REACH and CLP.

• Experience working directly with customers or external partners on trials, scale-up or technology transfer.

• The ability to explain technical results clearly to scientists, customers and commercial colleagues.

• A structured, self-driven way of working, and comfort with the pace and ambiguity of an early-stage company.

• Fluent written and spoken English.

• The confidence to take full ownership of the role from day one. You will set your own priorities, make decisions within your remit and drive projects to completion without close supervision, keeping the CSO informed rather than waiting for direction.

Nice to have

• Experience in both inks and coatings and plastics.

• Experience with textile dyeing or printing.

• Experience with organic pigments, natural colourants or other bio-based materials.

• Knowledge of food contact and product safety requirements, such as EU 10/2011, the Swiss Ordinance, EuPIA guidelines, EN 71-3 or ZDHC.

• Experience with quality systems such as ISO 9001, or with setting product specifications for a new product.

• An existing network in the European ink, coatings, masterbatch or textile industries.

What we offer

• A central role in bringing a new class of sustainable pigments to market, with real influence over which products we build and how.

• Direct work with the founding team and a short path from idea to decision.

• A small, highly skilled team of scientists across synthetic biology, fermentation, downstream processing, formulation and application.

• For earlier-career candidates, a role that can grow with the company. For senior candidates, the chance to build and lead the product function.

• Real autonomy and ownership of your work, and the chance to make a lasting impact at a fast-growing company developing new materials for industries that urgently need to change.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark. On-site is strongly preferred; hybrid working is possible for the right candidate.

Start date: As soon as possible

Reports to: Chief Scientific Officer

Employment: Full-time, permanent

Travel: Some travel to customers and partners within Europe

Right to work: Applicants must already have the right to live and work in Denmark. We are unfortunately not able to sponsor work visas at this time.

How to apply

Apply with your CV. Please highlight the pigment applications you have worked on and a technical problem you solved in a customer's process.

We review applications on a rolling basis and will fill the position as soon as we find the right person, so we encourage you to apply early.

We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are happy to answer questions about the role before you apply.

Sophion Bioscience is looking for an ambitious, customer-focused Vice President of Research & Development to lead and further develop our R&D organization.

This is a central leadership role with responsibility for Sophion’s technology strategy, product development execution, engineering capabilities, and R&D organization. You will ensure that priorities, resources, budgets, and development activities are managed with clarity and discipline, enabling us to deliver high-quality products that create measurable value for customers.

You will report to the CEO and as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will contribute to Sophion’s overall direction and continued growth.

About the role

As VP R&D, you will lead and develop Sophion’s multidisciplinary R&D organization, setting a clear direction and creating the structure, leadership, and ways of working needed to deliver on our ambitions.

You will translate product and portfolio priorities into clear R&D priorities, roadmaps, and resource commitments, ensuring alignment and accountability across the organization. Working closely with Innovation, Market & Product Management, you will ensure R&D brings strong judgment and execution discipline to the development of differentiated and commercially successful products.

A key part of your mandate will be to strengthen the R&D organization and its leadership. You will develop leaders, build effective teams, establish clear governance and decision-making, and create a culture of collaboration, ownership, and delivery.

You will attract, develop, and retain talented people and ensure that R&D continues to grow in capability, maturity, and performance.

About Us

Since 2000 Sophion Bioscience has pioneered Automated Patch Clamping for ion channel research. Today, we specialize in automated solutions for pre-clinical life sciences.

We work closely with academic institutions, contract research organizations, and leading biotech and pharmaceutical companies to create effective assays for screening and characterization. Our solutions empower the study of drug targets and candidates at the bench, reducing development time in discovery and reducing risk in clinical trials.

Through the continued development of our Automated Patch Clamp portfolio (QPatch & Qube) and our new Organ on a Chip platform (Ethica), we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis.

We are driven by curiosity, teamwork, and a genuine passion for helping scientists succeed. We work in an open and collaborative environment where people share knowledge freely, support each other across roles and borders, and take pride in doing things properly. Our culture is informal, trusting, and grounded in respect — for colleagues, customers, and the science we enable. Even as we grow globally, we remain a company where people feel welcome, included, and able to make a meaningful impact.

We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China.

What You'll Do

• Set and execute Sophion’s R&D and technology strategy in alignment with the company’s overall direction and priorities.

• Lead and develop the R&D organization, including its structure, leadership capabilities, ways of working, and competencies.

• Clearly communicate R&D priorities, progress, risks, and trade-offs across Sophion and to the Leadership Team and Board.

• Own the R&D budget and ensure resources are allocated to the activities that create the greatest strategic and customer value.

• Drive portfolio and resource management, translating product priorities into actionable development roadmaps and execution commitments while balancing short- and long-term priorities.

• Ensure customer needs inform development decisions by driving broad R&D engagement with the market, key opinion leaders, and key accounts.

• Strengthen development governance, decision-making, accountability, milestones, KPIs, and transparent reporting.

• Drive continuous improvement in product quality, performance, reliability, and maintainability.

• Work closely with Innovation, Market & Product Management to assess opportunities and convert agreed priorities into robust and commercially viable products.

• Maintain appropriate quality and compliance standards across R&D activities.

• Build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders

Who You Are

You are a strategic and hands-on R&D leader who can turn complex scientific and technical opportunities into high-quality products.

You bring clarity to complex situations and combine strong judgment with disciplined execution. You build strong teams, set clear priorities, use resources effectively, and deliver commitments.

You are engaging and decisive, and you build trust through transparency, communication, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through. You are comfortable moving between strategic questions and operational details without losing sight of R&D and company priorities.

We expect that you:

• Master’s degree in science, engineering, technology, or a related field.

• Proven R&D leadership experience in complex, multidisciplinary product development, leading leaders and sizeable teams of specialized engineers and scientists across hardware, software, firmware & bioscience.

• Strong communicator with the ability to set the agenda, shape strategy, and communicate in a clear direction across the organization and with customers and investors.

• Track record of taking products from concept to successful global market use.

• Experience from life science tools, diagnostics, MedTech, laboratory instrumentation, or similar quality-critical environments is preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to improve execution, prioritization, organizational capability, and product quality.

• Strong strategic, customer, communication, and decision-making skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions and deliver results.

• Strong interpersonal, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with professional English proficiency.

How to Apply

Please apply via LinkedIn.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact Helene Fife on hef@Sophion.com

Start Date

As soon as possible.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate. If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

_Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant or outsourcing company.

**Deliver with focus. Scale with intent 🚀

**Are you a delivery leader who knows how to guide enterprise customers through complex set-ups without over-engineering the journey? Do you care deeply about building scalable, repeatable SaaS delivery rather than one-off custom projects?

At Performativ, we’re building the infrastructure layer for modern wealth management. As our Engagement Manager, you’ll lead the enterprise rollout of our SaaS platform helping customers onboard successfully through structured delivery, clear communication, and lightweight technical engagement.

This is not a professional services consulting role. You won’t be buried in endless customer-specific code or heavy customizations. Instead, you’ll work cross-functionally to help customers adopt our product the right way: cleanly, securely, and in line with platform best practices so they can scale on top of us, not around us.

**What You Will Do

**

• Own enterprise set-up programs end to end (kick-off through go-live and hyper-care) against an agreed plan and scope (Statement of Work).

• Enable customers to integrate Performativ via standard platform patterns (APIs, SSO, configuration) without custom buildouts, working with product and engineering to flag gaps early and advocate for scalable paths.

• Own plan, scope, and change control, keeping scope tied to contract and change visible and decided rather than quietly absorbed, and support the Technical Program Lead on requirements, design documents, and acceptance-criteria sign-off.

• Run customer communication, cadence, and governance with reporting that keeps meetings short, and manage risk, dependency, and issue tracking (including customer-side).

• Lead a clean handover to Customer Success at go-live or hyper-care exit, including train-the-trainer sessions and supporting materials.

• Represent the program in internal capacity and exception reviews, bringing requests the plan cannot absorb back as options rather than committing on the spot.

• Build repeatable playbooks, documentation, and artefacts that make the next program faster. You will be measured on this, not only on your own delivery.

**How You Will Work

**You will run multiple programs at once, in a delivery pod alongside the Technical Program Lead, Integration Engineers, Data Migration Specialists, and Product Engineers. None report to you. Rather you get things done through clarity and relationships, not authority. You will report to the COO. This is an in-office role based at our Copenhagen office.

**What We're Looking For

**

• 7+ years in program or engagement management, consulting, product management, or another delivery-facing role, with a track record of leading complex, multi-stakeholder implementations end to end.

• Comfort being firm with customers on scope and timeline while keeping the relationship stronger for it.

• Any industry background welcome. Experience with enterprise customers (banks, asset managers, regulated industries), balancing urgency against long-term maintainability highly advantageous.

• Structured and highly organized, producing written plans, governance cadences, and reporting that stakeholders can act on.

• Broad technical literacy across enterprise SaaS delivery: API-based integrations, SSO and security configuration, and data migration and mapping, including enough SQL to read and question a mapping. You do not build the integration, but you understand it well enough to scope it, question it, and know when something does not add up.

• Ability to build working fluency in the customer's business domain fast: within 90 days, able to discuss topics such as advice and suitability workflows and customer reporting without a subject-matter expert in the room.

• ITIL Foundation, PMP or PRINCE2 Certification would be beneficial.

**Technical Fluency

**

• You’re not, necessarily, a developer, but you’re comfortable with APIs, data structures, auth flows (OAuth/SAML), and deployment models.

• You can dive into logs, payloads, and basic SQL or Python when needed to unblock yourself or a customer - but you prioritize scalable fixes over tactical workarounds.

• You advocate for platform-aligned solutions, not special cases.

**What This Role Is Not

**This role sits in operations, not engineering or commercial, and is project-based: once delivery is complete, you roll on to the next engagement. As a SaaS provider, we do not build bespoke software; delivery works within the bounds of the product.

**We Can Offer

**

• Trust and responsibility to shape how Performativ delivers for its largest customers.

• A competitive salary and benefits package.

• A fast-growing, VC-backed fintech scaleup, working alongside professionals from leading institutions (Goldman Sachs, McKinsey, BCG, Amazon and others).

• Career acceleration through professional development and leadership opportunities.

**Can you work at night, perform in a busy environment, do you have experience from packing or from a warehouse and do you have a good physique?

About the job**

As a warehouse employee you are an important part of the business. You will pack products for our customers from refrigerated, dry, green and frost areas. We use pick-by-voice, and you will be walking around the warehouse, picking and packing orders throughout your entire shift. This requires that you have a good physique.

The packing department consists of more than 40 different nationalities and since it is a multicultural area it requires that you speak and understand English.

Work hours

Nemlig operates 365 days a year, and for this position you will be working two fixed night shifts during the weekend.

We are offering a flexible part-time contract of 15 -25 hours per week, consisting of 2 night shifts of 7.5 hours.  Your average working hours will be between 15 and 25 hours per week, calculated over a planned period of at least 4 weeks. Usually, you will be scheduled for 15 hours per week, spread across 2 working days Saturday and Sunday night. During busy periods, we may change your work schedule one month in advance, increasing your working hours by up to 25 hours per week. It is therefore important that you are flexible during busy periods, e.g. Christmas and New Years.

Your working hours will be:

• Saturday night / Sunday morning: 22:00 Saturday to 06:00 Sunday

• Sunday night / Monday morning: 22:00 Sunday to 06:00 Monday

This is a weekend night position, and it is therefore important that you are able to work both Saturday and Sunday night shifts every week. Over time, there may be an opportunity to work additional night shifts during the week.

Please note: As part of the recruitment process, selected candidates will be invited to an interview  at 10 am on a weekday (Tuesday or Wednesday) followed by additional onboarding sessions at 11 am on a weekday (Thursday or Friday), too. Therefore it is important you are available om weekdays in the daytime for interview and onboarding.

Availability to attend the interview and all scheduled onboarding sessions is a requirement for the position.

Our expectations

We hire responsible employees who thrive in a performance environment and who are willing to go the extra mile.

Furthermore, we expect that you:

• Have a good physique

• Keep calm - even in stressful situations

• Speak and understand English

• Can work the fixed night shifts during the weekend

Experience with single items picking, working in a warehouse environment and using pick-by-voice systems is a plus, but not a requirement.

**WHY WORK AT JOE & THE JUICE

**JOE & THE JUICE is a people-centric food and beverage company built around culture, offering much more than just juice, sandwiches, and coffee.

We believe in four simple virtues that shape everything we do:

• Positive Attitude

• Inclusion

• Social Ties

• Growth

For us, this means that when you choose a cup-half-full mindset, welcome people from every background, build real friendships across the teams by creating or helping create great guest experiences, and use every day as a chance to learn something new, you become more than just a Juicer or staff member; like us, you continue to search and find purpose and meaning in what you do.

From your first day, you'll be part of an international network of people who support each other, celebrate wins together, and push each other to grow. You'll learn by doing and move through our Moneyball career path—our internal system that tracks your performance and fast-tracks you toward promotion. Most of our leaders have earned their stripes behind the bar (fun fact: over 75% of our employees started as Juicers!), so you will always be part of a company built on that same journey. If you love a fast-paced environment, music, and people, and you like the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that takes you across cities, countries, and roles.

**JOB SUMMARY

**The position as Payroll Specialist - Mid EU will be a part of our Financial Shared Services department, which also includes Accounting and Accounts Payables. The position will be embedded and report to the Global Payroll Manager in the HQ - Copenhagen, Denmark. This role provides potential for growth within the company and the role offers an exciting opportunity for the right candidate to develop their career within Joe & The Juice. The role is a full-time position.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• The overall responsibility will be processing monthly Payroll in the following markets: Belgium, France, Switzerland, Netherlands, Monaco and Germany (Note: all mid-EU payrolls are outsourced; you will be coordinating with a provider - for now; exception made for France and the Netherlands where it is done in-house).

• Fielding employee questions regarding pay.

• Responsible to onboard new joiners into payroll systems.

• Responsible to keep HRIS/employee data up-to-date, in cooperation with local HR teams, in regard to leave and absence, personal data, etc.

• Reconciling payroll data against accounting records, preparing and reviewing payroll-related bookings and journal entries, and supporting month-end close.

• Acting as the point of coordination between local HR, Finance and external payroll providers to ensure accurate and timely payroll delivery.

• Ad-hoc HR / Payroll tasks as necessary.

**WHO YOU ARE

**

• You have high attention to detail and a strong sense of confidentiality when handling sensitive employee data.

• You have strong communication skills and can liaise confidently with employees, HR, Finance and external payroll providers.

• You can manage competing deadlines across multiple markets and payroll cycles simultaneously.

• You have a proactive, problem-solving mindset and are comfortable working in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING

**

• Experience in multi-jurisdiction payroll, ideally covering 2 or more countries within the Mid Europe market (Belgium, France, Switzerland, Netherlands, Germany, Monaco).

• Fluent English required. Working proficiency in Dutch, German and/or French is a strong asset.

• Accounting experience, including reconciliation, bookings/journal entries and month-end close support.

• Solid understanding of payroll principles and local labor/tax compliance across two or more Mid Europe markets.

• Proficiency with Excel and payroll/HRIS systems; comfortable working with large datasets.

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 200 friendly faces come together!

• Fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• At JOE, we embrace a flat hierarchy that values every opinion, creating a welcoming space for your ideas and suggestions to thrive.

• Lively monthly social calendar filled with fun activities like running club, wine tasting, creative evenings, and Friday bars - there's always something exciting happening!

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

**ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Along the way, internal workshops and mentorship sharpen your skills, while exchange programs and international assignments can take you across our markets.

Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!

Developing our future sourcing strategy. Lead the development of our future sourcing strategy and participate in the negotiations with potential vendors, together with the Head of Corporate IT and business stakeholders.

Establishing the support model for the new NNF headquarters. Define and put in place the IT support model in preparation for the inauguration of the new headquarters in 2028.
